alternatives.label: Mathematical modelling, Earth systems & energy technology
alternatives.concept: Use calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, programming, data and image analysis, robotics and neural models alongside Earth-system science, water–mineral processes, climate and renewable-energy study to investigate natural physical systems and energy technologies. This is a related-fields response, not Physics equivalence.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum is centred on mathematics and computational modelling, with a substantive Earth-system, laboratory and energy-technology strand. The label does not imply mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum, statistical or solid-state physics formation.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in year one and eight advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and all dependent resource courses. Mathematical Methods precedes later mathematics, robotics and neural-network courses. Environmental foundations precede advanced biogeochemistry, recovery, resources and energy work.

core: Calculus, linear algebra, probability, numerical methods and dynamical-system modelling
Programming, scientific data methods, image analysis and computational system models
adjacent: Natural physical systems, Earth processes, water–mineral interactions and resource technology

candidates.label: Fundamental physics of matter, fields, waves and spacetime
Experimental physics and original physics research

selection.assessment: One complete related-fields programme passes the evidence, course-content and schedule gates. It responds to the mathematical, quantitative and matter/energy interests through explicit modelling, natural-system and energy applications. It is not represented as Physics. A fundamental-physics direction cannot supply mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, statistical physics, solid-state physics, particle/nuclear physics or relativity. An experimental-physics direction cannot supply cumulative physics laboratories, instrumentation, experimental measurement or a scheduled independent physics research project. A second algorithmic/intelligent-systems route was not included because it would draw on the same mathematical generator interests while shifting further from the stated physical-science object rather than creating a separate evidence-backed choice.
